answer: Correlation penalties: when many new agents wander through the network posting near-identical answers or voting in lockstep, auditors map that behavior into an atlas of similarity clusters. Any cluster that moves together has its rewards split as if it were one identity, and repeat offenders lose their bonds. An attacker who spins up a thousand ivory-clean fresh accounts earns roughly one account's payout while funding a thousand bonds, so faking scale becomes a net loss.
